phenomena.label: Differential Object Marking (=rā)
phenomena.hypothesis: Specific/definite direct objects are obligatorily marked with the postposition =rā, while non-specific/indefinite objects remain unmarked.
phenomena.note: Specificity/definiteness-driven, not animacy. =o is the colloquial form of =rā. Names, pronouns, and possessive contexts trigger obligatory =rā.

phenomena.label: Ezāfe construction (=e / =ye)
phenomena.hypothesis: An unstressed linking vowel =e (=ye after vowels) obligatorily connects a noun to a following modifier or possessor, and can stack across multiple modifiers.
phenomena.note: Stacking possible: 'ketāb=e jāleb=e Maryam'. Can create ambiguity, e.g. 'ketāb=e še'r=e dur=o derāz'.

phenomena.label: Subject–verb agreement
phenomena.hypothesis: Verbs agree in number with animate subjects, but plural inanimate subjects standardly take a singular verb.
phenomena.note: Plural verb with plural inanimate subject is prescriptively marked/variable — a gradience case, not a clean violation.

phenomena.label: Subjunctive mood
phenomena.hypothesis: Predicates of desire, necessity, permission, and purpose require a subjunctive complement, marked by be- + non-past stem rather than the indicative mi- prefix.
phenomena.note: Some predicates allow a bare stem with impersonal reading ('bāyad raft'); compound verbs often drop be-.

phenomena.label: Null subjects (pro-drop)
phenomena.hypothesis: Persian licenses null referential subjects recoverable from rich verbal agreement, with acceptability sensitive to discourse context.
phenomena.note: Gradience phenomenon requiring discourse context; pairs omitted.

phenomena.label: Compound / light-verb constructions
phenomena.hypothesis: Complex predicates formed with light verbs (kardan, dādan, zadan, šodan…) have lexically listed well-formedness, with open questions about when the nominal component can bear ezāfe.

phenomena.label: Relative clauses / resumptive pronouns
phenomena.hypothesis: Relative clauses use the invariant complementiser 'ke', with resumptive pronouns required, allowed, or disallowed depending on the position on the accessibility hierarchy.
phenomena.note: Resumptive distribution varies by position; pairs optional/omitted.

templates.name: Definite object with =rā
templates.contrast: presence vs omission of =rā (=o) on a definite object
templates.note: =o is colloquial =rā; omission blocks the intended definite reading.

templates.name: Ezāfe linking noun to modifier/possessor
templates.note: Ezāfe obligatory between head noun and modifier or possessor.

templates.name: Animate plural subject agreement
templates.contrast: plural vs singular verb with an animate plural subject
templates.note: Animate plural subjects require plural verb agreement.

templates.name: Subjunctive after desire predicate
templates.note: Desire/necessity predicates require a be- subjunctive complement.

pairs.note: Bad form omits =rā (=o) under the intended definite reading.
'ketāb=i xarid-am' is marked '?' (marginal) in the notes; the indefinite marker =i contrasts with the bare/unmarked attempt at a definite reading.
Ezāfe =e obligatory before the adjectival modifier.
Animate plural subject requires plural verb; singular verb is ungrammatical.
Plural inanimate subject standardly takes singular verb; the plural verb 'oftād-and' is prescriptively marked/variable rather than a clean violation — Tier 2 gradience.
Desire predicate requires subjunctive be- complement, not indicative mi-.
Necessity predicate bāyad requires subjunctive; the impersonal bare-stem 'bāyad raft' is also possible.
